problem: Flat end-to-end RL agents for object navigation cannot explore structured floor plans, ground language instructions, or reason at several abstraction levels; they get stuck, time out, or call done wrongly.
motivation: Finding objects in unseen homes needs room-level planning with memory, low-level locomotion and language grounding at once. The authors observe that a flat PPO agent barely progresses (about 20% SR with multiple objects) and that oracle room-level hints make the low-level task nearly solvable, so a high-level policy that supplies such hints should help.
key_idea: A hierarchical RL agent in which a meta-controller enhances the language instruction (e.g. 'Find the red ball, in the kitchen') to steer a low-level controller room by room, with a separately trained goal-assessment module handling language grounding and the done decision.
insight: Oracle instruction enhancements make the controller solve the task almost consistently, whereas without them it cannot learn, so the high-level room choice is the bottleneck. Soft termination (allowing repeated done) greatly improves sample efficiency, and the goal assessment module partly recovers this when hard termination is used (multi-object test 15% -> 40%). Room coverage roughly doubles versus the flat agent (e.g. 36.4% vs 12.6% on multi-object holdout), showing structured exploration.
method: Meta-controller: GRU policy over egocentric RGB and instruction; its discrete action space is a set of instruction enhancements (rooms). It acts every c steps, is trained with a frozen controller or with a perfect-controller simulation using a room-coverage reward (+0.1 new room, -0.01 slack).
Instruction enhancement interface: language ties the levels together loosely, so controller and meta-controller can be trained independently and generalize to novel instructions.

Low-level controller: policy over egocentric RGB, instruction and enhancement; actions are move forward, turn left, turn right and query. It is trained with oracle (shortest room path) enhancements and a geodesic-distance-improvement reward, slack -0.01 and success bonus 10.

Goal assessment module: a supervised classifier G(o,g) -> {0,1} that judges whether the instruction is satisfied. Query does not terminate the episode (soft termination); if G accepts and the agent is close, the original done is issued. Trained on random-policy data with 50% positive and 50% negative instruction pairs, and can be retrained for novel objects.
Soft termination training: done can be used multiple times during training, improving sample efficiency, and G filters invalid done actions at test time.

setting.backbone: PPO-trained GRU-based meta-controller and controller (from scratch) + supervised goal assessment classifier
setting.training_data: RL interaction in MiniWorld domestic environment, 102 training floor plans of 132 (30 holdout), 6 training objects; goal assessment data collected with a random policy; controller trained for about 5M steps
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, query/done; meta-controller picks discrete room enhancements
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle room-path enhancements used only for controller training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 30 holdout floor plans; 10 runs x 100 random episodes
numbers.backbone: PPO GRU meta-controller + controller + goal assessment

numbers_note: Custom MiniWorld environment, not a standard benchmark. Flat PPO baseline test SR is 44% (single) and 12% (multiple).
results: In the custom MiniWorld domestic task the hierarchical agent with goal assessment reaches 75% SR on unseen floor plans with a single object versus 44% for flat PPO, and 40% versus 12% with multiple objects. With soft termination it reaches 67%. It generalizes to unseen floor plans and, with only the goal assessment retrained, to unseen color/shape objects.
limitations: Evaluated only in a simple synthetic MiniWorld environment with abstract objects, not photorealistic simulators or real robots
Performance drops in dynamic environments with multiple objects; the goal assessment module errs on barely visible objects in a single frame
The set of instruction enhancements (rooms) is fixed and predefined
